Yapay zeka çiplerine yönelik güçlü talep, Nvidia'nın mali yılının üçüncü çeyreğinde gelirini ve net kârını iki kattan fazla artırdı. Şirket, beklentilerin üzerinde sonuçlar açıklarken gelecek mali yıla ilişkin gelir tahminini de yükseltti. Yönetim kurulu ise kurucu ortak Jensen Huang'ın CEO'luk görevine geri dönmesini planlamadığını duyurdu.
Nvidia, kurucu ortağı Jensen Huang'ın görevinden ayrılmasının ardından yatırımcıları rahatlatmaya çalıştığı ilk bilançosunda, 25 Ekim'de sona eren üç aylık dönemde 115,8 milyar dolar (105,4 milyar euro) gelir elde etti. Bu rakam, geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 103 artışa işaret ederken Wall Street beklentilerinin de üzerinde gerçekleşti.
Şirketin net kârı 65,3 milyar dolara (59,4 milyar euro) yükseldi. Hisse başına seyreltilmiş kazanç 2,70 dolar (2,46 euro) oldu. Tek seferlik kalemler hariç hisse başına 2,68 dolarlık (2,44 euro) kâr ise FactSet tarafından derlenen 2,48 dolarlık (2,26 euro) piyasa beklentisini aştı.
Nvidia hisseleri, salı günü piyasa kapanışının ardından yapılan işlemlerde bir ara yaklaşık yüzde 5 yükseldi.
Nvidia Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Harvey Jones, bilanço toplantısının başında yönetim kurulunun Huang'ın istifasını "oybirliğiyle kabul ettiğini ve kendisini CEO olarak yeniden göreve getirme niyetinde olmadığını" söyledi. Şirketin mali işler direktörü Colette Kress, yönetim kurulu kalıcı bir halef ararken geçici CEO olarak görev yapıyor.
Huang, salı günü sosyal medyada yaptığı paylaşımda, yönetim kurulunun şirketin, hissedarlarının, çalışanlarının ve ABD'nin çıkarları açısından bunu uygun görmesi halinde göreve dönmeye hazır olduğunu söylemişti.
Geçen hafta başlatılan "Jensen'ın yanında dur" başlıklı imza kampanyası, SpaceX ve Tesla CEO'su Elon Musk gibi Silikon Vadisi'nden isimlerin desteğini aldı. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump da Huang'ın geri dönmesini memnuniyetle karşılayacağını belirtmişti.
Reuters'ın haberine göre Huang, evlilik dışı ilişkilerinin ortaya çıkmasının ardından istifa etti. Bu ilişkiler arasında, Çin istihbaratıyla olası bağlantıları ABD istihbarat kurumlarınca incelenen Çinli bir iş insanıyla yaşadığı ilişki de bulunuyor. Çin, Huang'ı hedef alan bir casusluk operasyonu yürüttüğü yönündeki iddiaları reddetti.
Jones, yönetim kurulunun kalıcı bir CEO'yu mümkün olan en kısa sürede atamak istediğini ancak doğru adayı bulmak için ihtiyaç duyduğu zamanı kullanacağını söyledi.
Nvidia'nın veri merkezi gelirleri iki kattan fazla artarak 107,6 milyar dolara (97,9 milyar euro) ulaştı. Bu artış, yapay zekâ altyapısına yönelik yatırımların güçlü seyrini koruduğuna işaret ediyor.
Çip üreticisi, dördüncü çeyrek gelirinin yaklaşık 130 milyar dolara (118,3 milyar euro) ulaşmasını beklediğini açıkladı. Bu tahmin de Wall Street beklentilerinin üzerinde.
Söz konusu çeyrek, fazladan bir haftayı kapsıyor. Gelir tahmini ayrıca Nvidia'nın Çin'e veri merkezi işlemci çipleri satmayacağı varsayımına dayanıyor.
Nvidia, satışların maliyeti düşüldükten sonra gelirden geriye kalan payı gösteren düzeltilmiş brüt kâr marjının, üçüncü çeyrekteki yüzde 74,9 seviyesinden dördüncü çeyrekte yüzde 71 ila 72 aralığına gerilemesini bekliyor.
Kress, Nvidia'nın mevcut siparişleri üzerinde anlaşılan fiyatlardan karşılamayı tercih etmesinin kâr marjlarını geçici olarak daralttığını söyledi. Kress, marjların dördüncü çeyrekte en düşük seviyeye ulaşmasını, şirketin fiyatlarını yeniden düzenlemesiyle gelecek mali yılda toparlanmasını bekliyor.
Kress, yapay zekâ altyapısının finansmanına ilişkin daha temkinli bir yaklaşım sergileyerek Nvidia'nın gelecekteki yatırımlarında "disiplinli ve seçici" davranacağını söyledi. Şirket, veri merkezlerinin kurulması için gerekli arazi, enerji ve bina sıkıntılarının giderilmesine öncelik verecek. Ayrıca yatırım yapılabilir kredi notuna sahip müşterilerini kendi projelerini finanse etmeye teşvik edecek.
Nvidia, 2028 mali yılına ilişkin gelir tahminini de yükseltti. Kress, şirketin 2027 mali yılı için daha yüksek bir gelir tabanından hareketle, 2028 mali yılında gelirlerinin yaklaşık yüzde 75 artmasını beklediğini söyledi. Önceki tahmin yüzde 70 artış yönündeydi.
Kress, tahminin veri merkezlerinin ne hızla faaliyete geçebileceği, talebin ne kadar güçlü kalacağı ve müşterilerin finansman sağlayıp sağlayamayacağı gibi unsurları dikkate aldığını belirtti.
Kress'e göre ChatGPT'nin geliştiricisi OpenAI ve Claude'un geliştiricisi Anthropic gibi büyük yapay zekâ laboratuvarlarının, bu mali yılda Nvidia'nın veri merkezi gelirlerinin yaklaşık yüzde 15'ini oluşturması bekleniyor.
Kress, bilanço toplantısının sonunda, "Büyümemiz gerçek. Talebimiz hızlanıyor," dedi.
Öte yandan Nvidia'nın yönetim kurulu, ulusal güvenlik, ihracat kontrollerine uyum ve küresel ticaret risklerini denetlemek üzere kalıcı bir komite kurdu. Trump, salı günü Manila'da yaptığı açıklamada bunu "iyi bir fikir" olarak nitelendirdi.
ABD Temsilciler Meclisi'ndeki üç komite, salı günü yaptıkları açıklamada Huang ve Nvidia'nın hukuk işlerinden sorumlu yöneticisi Tim Teter'ın, kapalı kapılar ardında ve tutanağa geçirilecek görüşmelere katılmayı kabul ettiğini duyurdu.
Milletvekilleri, Nvidia'nın gelişmiş çiplerinin Çin'e nasıl ulaşmış olabileceğini inceliyor.
Huang'ın 1 Aralık'ta, Teter'ın ise 2 Aralık'ta ifade vermesi bekleniyor.
Associated Press'in (AP) konuyla ilgili bilgi sahibi iki kişiye dayandırdığı haberine göre Huang'ın ABD Senatosu Bankacılık Komitesi karşısında da ifade vermesi bekleniyor.

Nvidia Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Harvey Jones, şirketin eski Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) Jensen Huang'ı yeniden CEO'luk görevine getirmeyi düşünmediklerini bildirdi.
Nvidia, 2027 mali yılının üçüncü çeyreği olarak kabul ettiği 25 Ekim'de sona eren üç aylık dönemin finansal sonuçlarına ilişkin telekonferans düzenledi.
Şirketin Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Harvey Jones, buradaki konuşmasında, Nvidia'nın son derece güçlü bir şirket olduğunu, finansal performansının da bunu açıkça ortaya koyduğunu söyledi.
Yönetim Kurulunun 12 Kasım'da şirketin davranış kuralları, standartları ve kurum kültürüyle bağdaşmayan kişisel davranışlarının ortaya çıkmasının ardından Jensen Huang'ın başkanlık, CEO'luk ve yönetim kurulu üyeliği görevlerinden kendi isteğiyle istifa ettiğini duyurduğunu anımsatan Jones, Huang'ın istifasının oy birliğiyle kabul edildiğini ve kendisini yeniden CEO olarak görevlendirme niyetinde olmadıklarını aktardı.
Jones, Huang'ın istifasına ilişkin koşullar ve devam eden soruşturma hakkında herhangi bir açıklama yapmayacaklarını ve bu konudaki soruları yanıtlamayacaklarını belirtti.
Yeni CEO'nun belirlenmesi sürecinde şirket içinden ve dışından adayların değerlendirileceğini aktaran Jones, gelişmiş çip teknolojileri ve ulusal güvenlik dinamiklerinin sektörde büyük değişimlere yol açtığını, yeni CEO'nun bu koşulları çok dikkatli şekilde yönetmesi gerekeceğini ifade etti.
Jones, kalıcı CEO'nun mümkün olan en kısa sürede göreve getirilmesini istediklerini ancak doğru adayı bulmadan atama sürecini aceleye getirmeyeceklerini kaydetti.
Nvidia'nın geçici CEO'su ve Finans Direktörü (CFO) Colette Kress de iş açısından bakıldığında şirkette her şeyin alışılageldiği şekilde sürdüğünü belirtti.
Şirketin müşterileri, tedarikçileri ve iş ortaklarıyla iletişim halinde olduklarını anlatan Kress, "Hepsi de bizi yüzde 100 destekliyor. Müşterilerimiz, iş görünümüne desteklerini ve bu süreçte bize yardımcı olma isteklerini dile getiriyor. Ayrıca, arz ve talep arasındaki boşlukları daraltmak için tedarikçilerimizle de yakın bir işbirliği içinde çalışıyorlar." diye konuştu.

Savcı, bu 9 ismin 2820 sayılı Siyasi Partiler Kanunu'nun 112'nci maddesinde düzenlenen "oylamaya hile karıştırılması" suçu ile bir yıldan üç yıla kadar hapisle cezalandırılmasını talep etti.
İddianamede, 4-5 Kasım 2023'te Ankara Spor Salonu'nda yapılan CHP 38. Olağan Kurultayı'nda Divan Başkanı olarak görev yapan Ekrem İmamoğlu ve diğer şüphelilerin ortak hareket ederek, kurultayda oy kullanan bazı delegelere yönelik çeşitli usulsüz faaliyetlerde bulunduğu öne sürüldü.

“I love our country”: Jensen Huang’s apology comes amid escalating Nvidia probes.
On Monday, large trucks began circling the streets of Washington, DC, carrying billboards urging Congress to investigate the Trump administration’s ties with Nvidia’s disgraced CEO Jensen Huang.
“Jensen was in bed with a spy from China,” the billboards created by the Tech Oversight Project (TOP) alleged. “Trump was in bed with Jensen.” TOP is a nonprofit that describes itself as “dedicated to reining in Big Tech.”
Currently, Trump is supporting a campaign to bring back Huang as Nvidia’s CEO—despite many Republicans calling it a “ horrible idea. ” Breaking his silence, Huang issued a statement Tuesday saying he would be “honored” to return, but the board said reinstatement is not under consideration as an internal investigation into US spying claims remains ongoing. Huang used the moment to say that his interests align with the US’s, saying:
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia.
Trump may have learned as early as this spring that Huang was potentially the target of Chinese espionage, but the president claimed recently that he didn’t know Huang was potentially exposed to a Chinese spy as he was becoming a prominent part of Trump’s inner circle, CNN reported .
If Trump wasn’t adequately briefed, it raises question about whether the White House acted with “sufficient urgency” to address a serious espionage threat, CNN said. But if Trump is deflecting, an even “graver question” will emerge about why Trump didn’t act on information and instead continued to keep Huang close, CNN said.
Instead of distancing himself from the Nvidia CEO, Trump invited Huang to sit at the head table during a state dinner with China’s president Xi Jinping, and last month, Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science, the nation’s highest scientiﬁc honor, for his AI achievements.
“Not only has he continued to do nothing, he’s invited that very CEO into the White House and on state visits to China with him,” Sacha Haworth, TOP’s founder and CEO, told Ars. “And the question we all have to ask is ‘why on Earth would he do that?’”
What Trump and Nvidia knew—and when—have become central questions for some Republicans, as well as top Democrats who plan to investigate the scandal when they assume control of key committees in Congress next year. Andrew Yoon, head of research for a nonprofit called CivAI, which warns the public of dangers from AI, told Ars that Huang doesn’t need to be compromised by China to have endangered the US. Prioritizing boosting profits over national security alone is “pretty concerning.”
“I think the most notable thing here is that Jensen Huang has been at the absolute forefront of lobbying to be able to sell chips to China,” Yoon said. “He has leveraged his very deep relationships with government, especially President Trump, in order to be able to sell as many Nvidia chips to China as he can get away with. If he could be selling Blackwell chips to China, I’m sure he would be.”
Yoon noted that evidence suggests some Chinese AI models have been trained on Blackwell chips. Even with China’s push to prioritize domestic chipmakers like Huawei, Nvidia chips remain “indispensable” to China’s frontier AI goals, Yoon said. And national security experts fear that access to high-end chips will help China advance its military AI or gain economic ground.
The White House isn’t commenting on Trump’s relationship with Huang. Among the lawmakers accusing the Trump administration of “corruption” is Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), The Wall Street Journal reported . He has already asked the White House to “preserve all communications” between Trump and Huang.
Other lawmakers are “seeking more information about what Trump knew about the relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang,” the former Megaspeed CEO whom Huang admitted to having an affair with. They also want to know more about “the administration’s failure to stop artiﬁcial-intelligence chips from going to China,” WSJ reported, and Nvidia’s reportedly $25 million donation to the White House ballroom.
“It is not just an intelligence issue; it’s also a potential corruption issue,” Blumenthal said. “There needs to be a really penetrating, comprehensive investigation of all the possible compromises of our intelligence that may have occurred, but also… that Donald Trump is so high on the head of Nvidia, and now is potentially linked to intelligence compromises.”
Trump has profited off Nvidia’s success while in office, buying “millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares in his personal brokerage accounts since returning to oﬃce in 2025,” the WSJ reported. The White House maintains that the president has no role in managing his stock portfolio.
Other officials advising Trump on AI also benefited from relaxing export curbs, TOP said. On Tuesday, the group issued a report summarizing what the public knows about potential conflicts of interest of two Trump officials: former White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.
Haworth, TOP’s founder, told Ars she’s concerned that Sacks and Lutnick abused their power to convince Trump to let Nvidia sell cutting-edge technology to China, while standing to “gain astronomical amounts of money.”
“The public is outraged by Nvidia’s CEO for compromising our national security, but we didn’t get here because of Jensen Huang’s missteps alone,” Haworth said. If “Nvidia was knowingly doing business with companies tied to illegal chip sales and smuggling with China,” then “the Trump administration was asleep at the wheel,” she said.
“White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick were protecting their own fortunes rather than looking out for Americans,” Haworth said.
If the US fails to hold them accountable for alleged conflicts of interest, “it would send a signal that powerful men once again cannot be held to account and that powerful men are protecting powerful men,” Haworth said.
Detailing Sacks’ alleged conflicts, the group cited New York Times reporting that the former AI czar had long supported Huang’s stance that allowing Nvidia to sell more chips in China would help the US stay ahead in the AI race. After Sacks became Trump’s key AI advisor, Huang quickly forged a “tight bond” with him, and “both stood to benefit” from their push to sell chips to China, TOP reported.
Also notably, while advising the White House, Sacks opposed policies such as the Trump administration’s recent move to cut off China’s remote access to US-made chips through now-restricted Southeast Asian data centers. Citing Sacks’ alignment with Huang, TOP reported that after just one meeting with the two men, Trump decided to allow Nvidia to sell AI chips to China that the Biden administration had previously blocked.
Huang valued his alliance with Sacks, TOP noted, citing reporting that showed Huang declaring last year that Nvidia was “lucky” to have Sacks advising Trump. But TOP is concerned that the alliance was built on mutual financial interest and that Sacks took a part-time role in the Trump administration to avoid divestments or disclosure requirements that might have revealed the extent of his possible conflicts of interest.
TOP flagged two areas it believes warrant Congressional investigation. While advising Trump to embrace AI deregulation, Sacks and his firm, Craft Ventures, continued investing substantially in AI. Sacks also stood to benefit from pushing Trump to integrate AI into warfare and national security tools, TOP’s report said. Nvidia’s Q3 revenue has more than doubled, with income from data centers up 110 percent from last year, to $107.6 billion.
Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress announced the company’s Q3 earnings on Tuesday, without initially mentioning former CEO Jensen Huang or the details of his departure , or possible attempt at a return . texts.https://www.theverge.com/report/1035465/:
The board said it would not take additional questions on the call about Huang’s departure.
Starting Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, new board chair Harvey Jones said that when former CEO Jensen Huang resigned, “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”
Jones added, “We will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation.”
Huang had publicly floated the idea of returning earlier on Tuesday. In a statement posted to X , he wrote that he “did not live up to the standards expected of everyone” at the company, that he regretted his mistakes, and that he would cooperate with the Nvidia board’s investigation into his actions. He added that he’d be willing to return to the chief executive role if offered it, though a day earlier, the Nvidia board reportedly said it was not considering bringing him back. “NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company,” Huang wrote. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”
But since his November 12th resignation, Huang remains entangled in scandal. He’s reportedly had three affairs, two with subordinates at Nvidia, one with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset suspected of facilitating illicit chip sales . (Huang has pushed against restrictions on Nvidia chip sales in China.) He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st, and an internal company investigation is ongoing.
Tech industry heavyweights have still voiced their support for Huang, dubbing him “irreplaceable” and petitioning for his return. Some have cast doubt on the allegations that Alice Huang (no relation) was spying on behalf of China and painted the leaks about their relationship as a conspiracy against the former CEO. President Donald Trump, a close ally of Huang for much of the past year, has also backed him. On Monday, Trump said he “would not mind” Huang returning, adding that “I think he learned a big lesson — I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another.”
Trump’s closeness with Huang could also complicate things for Nvidia, however. The company has ramped up its lobbying in Washington, D.C., spending $5 million in 2025 and $4.7 million so far in 2026. But as Democrats prepare to take Congress, they’re planning to investigate Trump’s dealings with Big Tech and other industries, alleging potential corruption. “The election wasn’t very positive for AI, and [the news around Huang’s resignation] is only going to complicate things, especially for the company in particular but for AI as a whole going forward,” Brendan Glavin, director of insights at OpenSecrets, told The Verge in an interview last week.
Lior Prosor, managing partner at Deep33, a tech VC firm, said last week that he didn’t expect Huang’s resignation to pop the AI bubble, although Huang has had a significant hand in mobilizing funds for the AI infrastructure buildout in the U.S. Under Huang’s leadership in August, Nvidia entered into partnerships with six financial institutions for about $500 billion to fund such endeavors. “NVIDIA supplies roughly 75 percent of the AI compute hardware the industry consumes, and demand continues to dramatically outpace supply,” Deep33’s Prosor said in an interview with The Verge . “Neither its customers nor its competitors can easily replace the capabilities it provides, and the economic incentives driving the AI trade remain unchanged.”
Even so, a potential market cooling has some worried, as Anthropic’s IPO, slated to potentially be the largest of all time, is set for Thursday. The chipmaker had agreed to buy $10 billion in Anthropic shares via private placement, on top of a $10 billion funding promise Nvidia had already made last year.

Huang, yönetim kurulunun dönüşünün hissedarlar, çalışanlar, şirket ve ABD açısından en doğru seçenek olduğuna karar vermesi halinde CEO'luk görevine geri dönmeye hazır olduğunu dile getirdi.
Jensen Huang aynı açıklamada, Nvidia'da herkesten beklenen standartları karşılayamadığını ve özel hayatında ciddi hatalar yaptığını kabul etti. Yönetim kurulu açısından sorunlara yol açtığını belirten Huang, Nvidia yönetim kurulunun yürüttüğü bağımsız soruşturmayla iş birliği yapacağını da söyledi. Ancak Nvidia yönetimi Huang'ın çağrısına olumlu yanıt vermedi.
Nvidia Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Harvey C. Jones , şirketin finansal sonuçlarının ardından gerçekleştirilen yatırımcı görüşmesinde yönetim kurulunun Huang'ın istifasını oy birliğiyle kabul ettiğini ve Huang'ı yeniden CEO olarak görevlendirmeyi düşünmediğini açıkladı. Jones, Huang'ın şirketin davranış kuralları, standartları ve kurum kültürüyle uyumlu olmayan kişisel davranışlarının ortaya çıkmasının ardından başkanlık, CEO'luk ve yönetim kurulu üyeliği görevlerinden gönüllü olarak ayrıldığını belirtti.
Nvidia'da CEO'luk görevini geçici olarak şirketin CFO'su ve başkan yardımcısı Colette Kress yürütüyor. Yönetim kurulu ise kalıcı CEO için hem şirket içinden hem de dışarıdan adayları değerlendiriyor.
Nvidia yönetim kurulu aynı zamanda şirketin ulusal güvenlik ve ihracat kontrollerine ilişkin süreçlerini denetlemek için yeni bir komite oluşturdu . Komitenin başkanlığını Nvidia yönetim kurulu üyesi ve Goldman Sachs'ın eski başkan yardımcısı Suzanne Nora Johnson üstlenecek.
Reuters'a göre bu hamle, Huang'ın ayrılmasının ardından Nvidia'nın yönetim yapısında attığı ilk önemli adımlardan biri oldu. Huang'ın istifası, özel hayatına ilişkin ortaya çıkan bilgilerle birlikte Çin ile bağlantılı şirketlerle Nvidia arasındaki ilişkilerin de incelemeye alınmasına yol açtı. ABD'li yetkililer özellikle Huang'ın eski Megaspeed yöneticisi Alice Huang ile ilişkisini ve Megaspeed'in kısıtlamalara tabi Nvidia çiplerinin Çin'e yönlendirilmesinde rol oynayıp oynamadığını inceliyor. Megaspeed ise herhangi bir usulsüzlük yaptığını reddediyor.
Wall Street Journal'ın aktardığı bilgilere göre ABD Menkul Kıymetler ve Borsa Komisyonu (SEC) da Nvidia hakkında bir inceleme yürütüyor. İncelemenin kapsamı henüz netleşmiş değil; ancak şirketin yatırımcılara yaptığı açıklamaların yanıltıcı olup olmadığının değerlendirilen konular arasında olduğu belirtiliyor.
Öte yandan Huang'ın yeniden göreve getirilmesi için çalışanlar, yatırımcılar ve teknoloji dünyasından isimlerin destek verdiği bir kampanya da yürütülüyor. Huang'ın kendisi de dönüşe açık olduğunu açıkça ortaya koymuş durumda. Buna rağmen Nvidia yönetim kurulunun son açıklaması, şirketin şimdilik Huang sonrası döneme ve yeni bir kalıcı CEO arayışına odaklandığını gösteriyor.

The US secretary of state was speaking after Microsoft, major banks, and the National Security Agency were all affected by technical failures in recent days
US secretary of state Marco Rubio has sought to assure Americans that there’s “zero” information that the cascade of service outages – which have grounded flights, cut off work access, limited bank access and disrupted classified communications – are related to each other or to a malign actor.
In recent days, Microsoft , major US banks , American air traffic control systems and the National Security Agency have all been affected by technical failures and outages. Donald Trump has faced a groundswell of criticism as friends and foes alike demand the White House answer for the disruptions.
“We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind,” Rubio said.
He made the comments as he travelled with Trump for key meetings in the Philippines on Wednesday, before flying to the tech hub of Shenzhen in China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit.
Trump was dismissive when asked whether he was concerned about the outages on Tuesday. “It’s life. When you’re big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It’s fine,” Trump said in Manila.
The series of outages began on Thursday, when Microsoft’s email and other tools went down , paralysing millions of workers who rely on them. Microsoft traced the issue to “an earlier network capacity upgrade”.
Flights across the US were grounded the next day in the longest so-called ground stop since the September 11 attacks. The US Federal Aviation Administration blamed a router upgrade.
By Monday, the banks were in the spotlight, as customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts at several major financial institutions and the money transfer service Zelle after a technical issue at JP Morgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system. Chase said it was caused by “a software bug” and was “not cyber-related”.
The same day, United Airlines said it had resolved an internal system outage that delayed departing flights.
Then on Tuesday, an internal network that the National Security Agency uses to communicate classified information was offline after what the agency described as “routine maintenance”.
Karoline Leavitt, Trump’s former press secretary, said the White House needed to do more to explain the situation.
“What I would say to the White House is: transparency is key,” Leavitt said on Fox News. Later, she praised the White House for having director of national intelligence Jay Clayton address the outages in an interview on Fox Business Network.
“Looking very diligently across the landscape, we are not seeing this as a cyber-attack incident,” Clayton said, explaining that the US government believes the incidents were caused by security upgrades that took longer than planned or encountered unexpected hiccups.
Democrat Mark Warner, the chair of the Senate intelligence committee reiterated that message, saying “there is no indication that these incidents are the result of a cyberattack, foreign interference, or some coordinated effort.
“AI is making it possible to identify vulnerabilities across enormous numbers of systems at unprecedented speed, creating enormous pressure on companies and government agencies to patch those vulnerabilities immediately, often all at once, putting tremendous strain on systems that weren’t built to handle that pace of change.
“The evidence so far points toward legitimate efforts to secure our systems, not malicious activity.”

Waymo robotaxis are no longer allowed to operate on California freeways after the state’s Department of Motor Vehicles restricted the Alphabet-owned company’s operations following several incidents that raised safety concerns.
California’s DMV, which regulates the testing and deployment of autonomous vehicles in the state, issued the operational restrictions on Waymo on November 11. However, the restrictions weren’t made public until Tuesday. San Francisco Business Times was the first to report the order.
The DMV confirmed the new restrictions to TechCrunch, stating that the department took action after three Waymo autonomous vehicles entered an active construction closure on U.S. Route 101 near Burlingame, and another separate incident involving California Highway Patrol vehicles on Highway 280 in San Francisco.
Waymo has complied and is preventing its robotaxis from accessing freeways in any of the markets it operates in, including those outside of California. Waymo currently has commercial operations in 15 U.S. cities.
The DMV said Waymo’s freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety.
“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present, despite a prior restriction and corrective actions implemented following similar incidents that occurred on May 18, 2026,” according to an emailed statement sent to TechCrunch.
The DMV said the restrictions will remain in place until Waymo can demonstrate that it has taken “effective corrective actions” to address the deficiencies.
Waymo spokesperson Dana Gallagher told TechCrunch the company has temporarily restricted freeway operations across its other operating markets to evaluate its performance.
“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do,” Gallagher said in a statement. “Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”
Waymo began offering freeway rides in late 2025 , a commercial milestone that has been central to its expansion in major metro areas. Freeway access allows Waymo to connect riders to airports and other destinations more efficiently, slashing travel times by avoiding slower surface streets.
That has been particularly important in the San Francisco Bay Area because Waymo’s service area stretches from the city south to Silicon Valley. Freeway access has dramatically shortened trips across the Peninsula that previously took 45 minutes or more than an hour.
In May, Waymo abruptly stopped operating on highways. The company didn’t cite a specific reason at the time, but several social media posts showed Waymo robotaxis driving through traffic cones and struggling to navigate construction zones.
Waymo robotaxis returned to freeways in July after the company said it updated the self-driving software system to improve performance around freeway construction zones.

Over the past week, anyone could be forgiven for wondering whether a Diehard IV –style cyberwar had finally arrived in the US.
Across just four consecutive business days, a mass Microsoft exchange outage broke IT services for thousands of companies , a Federal Aviation Administration tech screwup grounded airplanes across the country, a software problem affecting JPMorgan Chase caused another round of disruption, a United Airlines system glitch delayed flights yet again, and an NSA classified network’s downtime left the agency’s staff sitting at home waiting to return to their office at Fort Meade. In the midst of a US war with Iran and rising fears of AI-enabled hacking , this still-unfolding comedy of IT errors colliding across American infrastructure felt to plenty of observers like more than a coincidence.
Yet there’s still no evidence that any one of these clustered technological failures were related, much less caused by hackers. Their improbable, sequential timing left Americans anxiously doomscrolling for signs of foul play. But in cases like these, it’s the job of cybersecurity analysts (and reporters at WIRED) to determine—vibes aside—whether the latest tech outage was actually an accident or the result of a cyberattack.
The baseline for that fact-finding, as anyone tasked with investigating these incidents will tell you, is that the vast majority of these digital breakdowns are not the result of malicious intent but rather casualties of IT admins’ constant war to keep computer systems from collapsing under the weight of their own complexity.
“I’ve just seen enough times where we thought maybe it’s a cyberattack and it turns out it’s not. Sometimes it will be, but typically not,” says Matthew Prince, CEO of the internet infrastructure company Cloudflare. “Right now, most of what we’re seeing is the standard background noise. Stuff breaks, and that’s just the nature of complex systems.”
So in the interest of soothing the country’s rattled nerves and helping us all find ground truth amid seemingly endless tech catastrophes, we at WIRED present our general guide to determining whether a tech outage is the result of a cyberattack. So take a breath—maybe open the bunker door to let in some fresh air—and read on.
The process of determining the cause of an IT service outage should begin with the assumption that it was an accident, says cybersecurity researcher Doug Madory.
As the head of internet analysis at the network security firm Infoblox, Madory says he monitors as many as a dozen network outages a day. Only around “one in a thousand,” he says, turns out to have been caused by hackers. “One's default position should be that it isn't a cyberattack,” he says, “unless there is some concrete evidence to the contrary.”
Given the rarity of cyberattacks compared to outages as a whole, it’s wise to look at other potential causes first. “Most big outages that look like attacks are self-inflicted,” says João Tomé, the internet research editor at network data company IPinfo. (In response to WIRED’s questions, Tomé also wrote his own guide for distinguishing outages from cyberattacks.) The usual suspects, he says, include “a bad update, a configuration change, a cable cut, or a power failure.”
In the scramble to understand what’s really happening with a given outage, it can sometimes be difficult to tell which sites and services are actually down. And there can be a few reasons for this muddled picture. Sometimes, an outage occurs within a foundational service like a big cloud provider. Major downtime within Amazon Web Services , for example, can cause a cascade of other failures among the company’s customers, who are all dependent on that infrastructure.
In other cases, multiple services can seem to be having outages and producing errors but are functioning normally and only having problems when they interact with an entity that’s down. This appears to have been the case in this week’s bank outage: Multiple banks appeared to be having issues, but they all seem to have been linked to certain inter-institutional transactions that involved JPMorgan Chase. Another good example of this scenario is situations where it may appear that multiple wireless carriers are struggling, but all of the failed calls actually involve one network that’s having an outage.
On top of these, there are also scenarios where one or more large services are down, and false (typically accidental or anecdotal) reports of additional outages create further confusion and opacity.
It can all feel overwhelming, even impossible, to attempt to parse these situations yourself—but there is a concrete place to start. If you think a website or service from a major tech company may be down, look for acknowledgment of the situation on their verified social media accounts or in the “newsroom” press release section of their websites. And keep in mind that you can find these pages and social media accounts through search engines, so you definitely don’t need to be familiar with every company’s communications strategy. Use this same approach for government agencies and other institutions.
Another concrete and vital source of information that you can find through search engines is what’s often known as “status dashboard” pages. Large digital platforms specifically offer these informational pages to provide transparency into whether different components of their service are functioning normally or dealing with issues. In a major incident, companies often thread incremental updates about system restoration on the status dashboard. AWS , Google Cloud Platform , and Microsoft Azure all offer these landing pages, and there are similar ones for other services like Meta business products , Google Workspace , telecom companies, AI companies, and so on.
When a cascading tech failure causes outages across many services at once, and the point of failure isn’t clear, sources of network data that monitor the internet at a broad scale can also help determine the underlying issue. Amanda Meng, a research scientist at Georgia Tech who helps run its Internet Outage Detection and Analysis service, or IODA, points to not only IODA’s own data—and its social media accounts on BlueSky and Mastodon —but also tools like Cloudflare Radar and Watch the Net . Infoblox’s Madory also posts his own findings about network outages on his social media accounts .
When IODA sees evidence of a network disruption, “we’ll look at the timing of it, the start, the end, the network affected, anything we can find out about it, and then try and connect it with what we see from reporting,” Meng says. That scope, location, and timing of an outage can help determine a suspected cause, whether it’s a single network that might be the victim of a buggy update, a region cut off by damage to a fiber optic cable or, in rarer instances, a cyberattack or even a government purposefully cutting off internet access to its citizens to stifle protests.
Even with those network clues, however, Meng advises returning to step two: Once an affected service is identified, its actual owners are often the best source to monitor for updates. “Usually the operators have the most information about what's actually going on,” she says.
Most often, mea culpa updates from companies or government agencies confirm an outage is caused by a tech mishap. In the rarer cases when that downtime results from an actual cyberattack or hacker breach, however, the hackers responsible often claim responsibility in some form.
Ransomware gangs, perhaps the most common source of serious malicious internet disruption, publicize their breaches on dark web pages that list their targets for the purposes of extortion, sometimes with a countdown timer designed to pressure victims to pay before they leak stolen information. Meaning and use of word has become more important in age of AI chatbot, says dictionary
In a world where the line between people and machines is more blurred than ever, Cambridge dictionary has sided with natural intelligence for its word of the year: human.
Breakthroughs in artificial intelligence – led by the arrival of ChatGPT three years ago – have made the question of what it means to be human as vexed as ever, but the dictionary has drawn a firm line with its choice of the word of 2026, defining “human” as “having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines”.
AI advances have spurred questions about whether computers can achieve consciousness, with the evolutionary biologist Richard Dawkins among those who answered in the affirmative, saying he was “left with the overwhelming feeling that they are human”. Sceptics, on the other hand , argue that there is a vast difference between how a human brain evolves and how an AI system is built.
Cambridge dictionary said the meaning and use of “human” had become more important in the age of the chatbot. Colin McIntosh, an editor of the dictionary, said AI was “changing the way we talk about being human” and had led to the word of the year being deployed to distinguish our work from that of advanced computer systems. “Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking has made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI: from top mathematicians to teachers of young children,” he said. “A recent increase in compounds such as ‘human-made’ highlight how the word has come to distinguish works or qualities of people, as distinct from AI.”
Prof Rachel Adams, an expert on AI governance and human rights at the University of Cambridge, said : “AI brings us back to questions that we’ve asked for millennia: who are we, what does it mean to be human? The answer to these questions has never been fixed or stable, but the act of asking it is something we have in common.”
Other tech-related words were on the shortlist: “agent”, the term for an AI system that can operate – sometimes alarmingly – without human control, and “analogues”, relating to non-digital activities. A non-tech contender was “wholesome”, a word to describe something which is likely to improve your life either physically, morally, or emotionally.
Earlier this month, “mogging” – meaning to outperform or outshine someone or something – was named the Collins word of the year .
Tech-adjacent words also stood out among the new additions to the Cambridge dictionary. “Looksmaxxing”, describing the act of making oneself as physically attractive as possible, which has been associated with the online manosphere , and “aura farming”, another term often encountered on social media, which refers to “the activity of doing things with the intention of showing a personality that people admire and think is attractive and interesting”.
The former UK prime minister Keir Starmer made the news late last year when some social media users wondered “why he was aura farming” with his TikToks ; Andy Burnham also appears to be attempting to master the art after becoming prime minister.

Watch: Marco Rubio says recent tech outages are 'completely unrelated' to one another
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed widespread concerns online that the series of recent tech outages in the past week are connected, telling reporters there was "zero evidence" of any link.
Rubio acknowledged that "people are fearful" the spate of outages, which included all flights being grounded in the US and widespread disruptions to banking, Apple and Microsoft services, could be linked or part of a plot.
"We are not under systemic attack," he said. "These events, one has nothing to do with the other, they are not inter-related."
Cyber-security experts have agreed that there is no evidence linking the outages, and many of the issues appear due to updates to old infrastructure.
In the past week, there has been a massive Microsoft outage , an apparent tech glitch which grounded all US flights for hours, and issues for the National Security Agency, outages affecting the biggest US banks and Apple.
Every affected company or agency has said the issue was not cyber-related and not the work of an outside actor.
Rubio's comments came hours after US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton also addressed the issue, telling Fox News the outages were not the product of a cyber-attack. He explained "lots of institutions" are patching or upgrading systems, which has caused some disruption.
Rubio was asked whether the Trump administration was concerned public fears could lead to stockpiling or a run on the banks.
He said the best way to combat such fears was for the US government to share everything they know with the American people.
"Every indicator we have is that every single one of these events has an explanation or a cause that has nothing to do with a cyber-criminal, has nothing to do with a hostile actor or another country," he said.
Technology-related disruptions have happened almost daily since Thursday, when a Microsoft outage disrupted many of its services, including email.
The next day, the US Federal Aviation Administration halted flights across the US for more than four hours with a rare national ground stop. It was the longest halting of flights since the 11 September 2001 attacks on the US.
The US transport secretary said the issue was technical and caused by a copper wire upgrade and outdated equipment.
On Monday, a United Airlines technology failure delayed about 150 flights and a JPMorgan Chase software problem disrupted service at the biggest and most utilised banks in the US.
Both United and Chase said a software issue was behind the glitch.
Apple users were impacted by outages affecting iCloud and Apple Pay on Tuesday. The company said the cause was not a cyber-attack but the outage was triggered by an an internal update.
The same day, a highly classified network used by the US National Security Agency (NSA) for internal communications also went offline for a period of time.
Passengers wait to check in at Los Angeles International Airport as flights resume after being grounded for several hours on November 13 due to a major communications outage.
Cybersecurity experts say there is no evidence connecting the Microsoft, airline, and bank disruptions from the last five days.
Kris Beevers, CEO and co-founder of the network and infrastructure management company NetBox Labs, acknowledged the circulating theories on social media linking the barrage of outages.
"There is something more ordinary, and more important to understand: the infrastructure that runs the world is changing faster than ever, and change is risk. Much of it is 30 to 40 years old, with decades of technical debt, and it's now being asked to change very quickly."
"It's putting more strain on these legacy networks, and it's also creating real urgency around security," he said.
"Our customers are the amazing teams behind these networks at airlines, banking, energy, and retail who are essentially doing heart surgery on a global scale to get these networks back up and running quickly."
Vice President of Threat Intelligence for Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, Sherrod DeGrippo, said: "What this week really underscores is how tightly coupled, and fragile, our core digital infrastructure is, where a single software bug or router failure can cascade nationwide."

Waymo has temporarily suspended its driverless vehicles from operating on all US freeways, the company has said.
The decision comes after California banned Waymo's driverless taxis from state freeways following a series of recent traffic incidents.
California's Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) cited an "imminent hazard to public safety" for the ban, noting an incident this month in which several driverless Waymo vehicles entered an active construction zone on US Route 101.
Waymo said it was working with state officials "diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations", adding that no injuries or collisions were reported following the incident on US Route 101 south of San Francisco.
California's DMV said Waymo's driverless taxis presented a risk "due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present".
In another incident earlier this month, footage widely seen on social media appeared to show a Waymo car trying to overtake patrol vehicles that were deliberately slowing the pace of traffic on a San Francisco highway.
The California ban, which came into effect on 11 November, would remain in place until Waymo "demonstrates to the department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions".
A Waymo spokesperson said: "In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance."
Data on Waymo's website suggests that its cars, compared to human drivers, are involved in 95% fewer crashes resulting in serious injury.
Waymo currently operates driverless taxis in 15 US cities, but only offered freeway rides in a handful of those locations, including San Francisco, Los Angeles and Miami.
The company's driverless taxis can continue to operate on regular city streets.
In May, Waymo recalled thousands of its self-driving cars in the US over a software issue that could allow vehicles to drive into flooded roads.
In the same month, multiple Waymo cars were spotted driving around a cul-de-sac in Atlanta, Georgia , in the early hours of the morning.

California authorities have declared self-driving cars an ‘imminent hazard to public safety’ after traffic incidents.
Waymo has paused its driverless taxi services on freeways across the United States after California temporarily banned the ride-hailing platform on the state’s highways over safety concerns.
A spokesperson for the California-based company – a subsidiary of Alphabet, Google’s parent company – said it has “temporarily restricted commercial freeway rides in all markets where we operate that service”, but it is “continuing freeway testing with trained autonomous specialists behind the wheel”.
Waymo implemented the suspension last Wednesday, according to the spokesperson, but they did not say how long it would last.
Along with California, the driverless vehicles will pause highway services in Phoenix, Austin and Miami. Waymo offers rides on city streets in areas including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver.
The spokesperson said the suspension would allow the company to “evaluate our performance” following incidents in California and that it prioritises safety.
One incident on November 6 went viral after video captured on a San Francisco highway showed a Waymo vehicle speeding towards and attempting to pass two police cars, even as their lights were flashing in an intentional bid to slow traffic.
The officers were driving behind a slow-moving construction truck.
The episode led the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) to temporarily ban Waymo vehicles from its highways, effective from November 11.
The DMV, which is responsible for road safety, said its decision was also prompted by a November 5 incident, when three Waymo autonomous vehicles drove into a construction zone in the San Francisco Bay Area.
Waymo said the construction zone incident did not result in injuries or collisions.
DMV spokesman Jonathan Groveman said in a statement that “similar incidents” occurred on May 18.
“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” he said.
The restrictions “will remain in place until Waymo demonstrates … it has taken effective corrective actions”, the statement read.
Waymo completes half a million trips each week and says it has demonstrated a 95 percent reduction in serious crashes as compared with human-driven vehicles.
It has been testing its vehicles in London since 2016, and has plans to expand into Munich and Madrid in 2027.

Bezos said that he was immediately drawn to Robert Pattinson’s performance during screen tests.
Robert Pattinson’s casting as James Bond made enough sense given his recent work with director Denis Villeneuve, who’s making the franchise’s next film over at Amazon. But it turns out that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos played a significant role in making the final decision, too.
During Semafor ’s Silicon Valley and the World conference today, Bezos said that he was “heavily involved” in the process of casting the newest 007:
We ran a really tight process and we made the final decision on Friday. There was a big group initially, and we down-selected to five finalists. Then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists, and it was really interesting — full costume, real sets, other actors. We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists, and then we got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all those screening tests, and reviewing all of that. And all of the actors were extraordinarily talented.
By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing, but there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances. It was kind of immediately undebated. Denis — the director — we all sort of gravitated to Rob. By the way, initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him, just because he’s already so famous. We sort of thought, ‘maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown.’ But in the screen test, it was so obvious. He is James Bond.
It’s not exactly surprising that a studio leader would want to have a say in casting the new face for one of their most lucrative franchises. But with Bezos being so hands-on, one can only image what this new era of Bond films will look and feel like once Amazon starts releasing them in theaters.

Speaking at an event in California, the Amazon CEO said he was originally "biased against" Pattinson - who starred in many blockbuster films like Batman and the Twilight series - "because he's already so famous".
The role of 007 has typically gone to an actor who is not as well known at the time of casting. But Bezos said in screen tests, "it was so obvious he is James Bond".
This will be the first 007 film in the official series not under the creative control of the Broccoli family, who had overseen the franchise since the first movie in 1962. Amazon purchased MGM, which co-owns the franchise, in 2022.
'Good Bond vibes' - Hollywood locals react to Robert Pattinson cast as new 007
"There was something special about Rob", Bezos said at Semafor Silicon Valley & The World Event on Tuesday.
Pattinson was unveiled as the franchise's seventh James Bond on Monday, taking over from actor Daniel Craig. He will star in the 26th Bond movie, due to be released in 2028.
In a statement, the London-born actor said: "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime."
The next Bond film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, but its title and exact release date have not yet been announced.
The announcement comes after years of intense speculation about who will take over from Craig in one of the most high-profile - and highly scrutinised - roles in entertainment.
Robert Pattinson was unveiled as the franchise's seventh James Bond on Monday
Several other actors, including Josh O'Connor, Callum Turner and Jack Lowden, were reported to be in the frame for the role as screen tests took place in recent weeks.
But Amazon MGM ultimately went with a household name, choosing a more bankable movie star who is widely seen as a safe pair of hands.
"We ran a really tight process and made the final decision on Friday," Bezos said.
There were five finalists who went through "real, old-fashioned screen tests", acting out three different scenes in full costume, with real sets and other actors, he said.
"By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing. But there was something special about Rob and his performance," Bezos added. "It was immediately un-debated. Denis [Villeneuve], the director … we all gravitated toward Rob."
The pick comes amid widespread Hollywood cuts and consolidation, with studios struggling to get people into cinemas.
Hollywood insiders have said Pattinson was viewed as a safe pick to bring audiences in, rather than taking a risk on a new actor who could grow with the franchise.
"Maybe he's boring. Maybe Hollywood would be passing up a chance to anoint a badly needed new star. But with so much at stake for everyone involved, that all makes him the obvious pick," Hollywood journalist Matthew Belloni, who predicted the pick, wrote in his newsletter.

BBC comedy Ann Droid explored the possibility of a human (played by Sue Johnston) having an AI robot as a live-in carer (Diane Morgan)
"Human" is the Cambridge Dictionary's Word of the Year — defined as "having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines".
"The growth of AI means it is now necessary to explicitly say 'human' for things that once could only be done by humans," said chief editor Colin McIntosh.
Examples of current usage included actors Scarlett Johansson challenging "an assault on human creativity" and Matthew McConaughey protecting himself against unauthorised digital reproduction of his voice or image.
"The measure of AI's success should be how much it improves human lives," said Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates on learning about the dictionary's choice.
McIntosh said dictionary editors had to be on top of how words could change over time "to reflect what people say and what they write".
His research revealed a four-fold use of the word human since 1900.
"'Man' used to be used in this sense a lot more, but now it is not acceptable to use 'man' to mean men and women," he added.
"Human didn't come into use in Middle English until the 14th Century, from a French word. Shakespeare used it, but after that it was very restricted in use."
There had also been an increased use of compound words such as human-made and human-driven, to distinguish the works, qualities and skills of people from AI.
"Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking has made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI, from top mathematicians to teachers of young children," said McIntosh.
Oscar-winner Matthew McConaughey was the first actor to use trademark law to protect their likeness from AI misuse, according to his lawyers
Gates recently made the case for "human reserved jobs" , external , such as caregiving, and reiterated his call for a robot tax to help fund training for people who lose their jobs to AI.
Other examples included the Nobel Prize in Physics laureate Geoffrey Hinton, who has been described as the godfather of AI, who warned "we're creating alien beings. I'm willing to be selfish and choose humans".
Pope Leo XIV has spoken of new forms of "dehumanisation" , external and the "pressing duty to remain profoundly human".
"Right now our understanding of humanity is changing," said Dr Tom McClelland, a philosopher of science at the University of Cambridge.
"We're trying to understand the difference between a human mind and an artificial mind, between living beings like us and artificial beings that we're creating. What sets us apart? Is it consciousness, creativity or compassion?"
When we want to specify something is made by humans and not machines or AI, we now need to say it, said Colin McIntosh
In response to the surge in AI-created content , academics are hoping to develop a universally recognised symbol to denote something that is "human made", similar to the "Fairtrade" label that emerged in the 1980s.
Prof Rachel Adams, an expert on AI governance and human rights at the University of Cambridge, said: "AI brings us back to questions that we've asked for millennia — who are we? What does it mean to be human?
"AI is going to be a profound test for humanity. There's a real risk that it deepens existing inequalities, but it also has the potential to solve them."

British musician backs Not AI’s To Take campaign, saying Albanese government has ‘a duty to protect Australian artists and their work’
Aria awards 2026 red carpet: Tame Impala, Baker Boy, G Flip and more – in pictures
Elton John has made a surprise appearance at the 2026 Aria awards to draw attention to Not AI’s To Take , a major campaign backed by the creative and media industries calling on the Australian government to protect copyright law in the face of lobbying from AI companies.
Delivering a pre-recorded message at Australian music’s biggest night on Wednesday, the British singer backed the new campaign, which is calling on the Albanese government to ensure Australian artists are reimbursed and consulted by AI companies interested in using their works for AI training.
“I have long admired the talent and creativity of Australian artists,” John said. “So I want to send an important message to the Australian government. You have a duty to protect Australian artists and their work. Don’t let AI use any Australian artist’s work without full permission. Please, protect the next generation of Australian artists. Thank you.”
Australian musicians Jack River , Dobby, Josh Pyke and KLP also addressed the room at Sydney’s Hordern Pavilion on behalf of Not AI’s To Take, joining the likes of Jimmy Barnes, Paul Kelly and Peter Garrett who were among the artists who launched the campaign this week.
“It is not just lyrics and songs from Yothu Yindi, Missy Higgins, Gurrumul and Jimmy Barnes – you’ll be handing over Elton John , Beyoncé and the Beatles’ work too,” Dobby said. “Do not let Australia be the weak link that lets the world down.”
Not AI’s To Take is being supported by dozens of groups representing the recording, writing, publishing, film, television and media industries, including news outlets such as News Corp, Foxtel, Seven Media and Guardian Australia. The campaign warns that changes demanded by AI giants could put the $70bn creative industry and its 600,000 workers at risk.
“When Peter Garrett, The Guardian and Newscorp are all singing from the same song sheet, the Parliament should take notice,” said Greens senator Sarah Hanson Young in a statement.
The Australian Recording Industry Association (Aria) is also backing the campaign, emblazoning the slogan on a billboard at the Hordern Pavilion on Wednesday.
“I can’t just go and film a movie at the movies. I can’t do whatever I want with other people’s IP,” musician Ben Lee told Guardian Australia on the Aria red carpet. “Corporations should be subject to the same laws. So if AI companies want to train on Australian music, it’s simple: pay us.”
Rapper Miss Kannina told Guardian Australia: “The Australian government doesn’t care about anybody but the billionaires, and they don’t care about artists especially. Any kind of opportunity the Australian government can get to make money, they fucking will.
“If you’re using datacentres and AI and shit like that, you’re not really an artist,” she added. “I think the Australian government would do a lot better putting a lot more money and time into communities and lower socioeconomic communities to do music programs and to really lift up the Australian music industry, because honestly, this thing is hanging by a fucking thread.”
Multiple music figures used their Aria speeches to address the threat of AI. Bluey composer Joff Bush, who won the award for best children’s album, paid tribute to the “real life human beings” who contributed to the show’s soundtrack, while Tim Minchin delivered a rousing speech in defence of “shitty, fucked-up, striving, stumbling, needy, petty, hopeful, heartfelt, fucking humanness”.
“Art is the way we reach out to one another, and it is defined and made beautiful by the glorious messiness of its human creators. This will only remain true if we assert it as true and act accordingly,” he said.
“Which is to say, AI can suck my balls,” he added to cheers.
Danny Rogers, the co-founder of Laneway festival, used his win for best music festival to call for urgent action.
“Original music and live music simply don’t exist without incredibly talented, dedicated and creative human beings,” Rogers said, adding: “The misuse of AI poses a real threat to our industry and things could change much faster than anyone realises. We simply cannot take human creativity for granted. We need to protect the people who make music we all love.”
While the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, has declared it would be “theft” if creatives weren’t paid for their work, and that artists “need to be compensated”, some AI companies have argued it is too difficult to make individual licensing deals under existing copyright law. AI companies have said they need legal certainty on the copyright issue before investing and training models in Australia, with Anthropic putting forward an “opt-out” model to scrape creative works unless a rightsholder objected.
A spokesperson for the attorney general, Michelle Rowland, told Guardian Ausrtralia on Tuesday that the government was “committed to supporting” creatives, and pledged any copyright changes would “deliver meaningful control and fair compensation”.
The government is expected to unveil a long-awaited legislative package on AI in late 2026 or early 2027, with proposals around datacentres, online safety, productivity and copyright.

Waymo self-driving taxis are no longer driving on highways after the California Department of Motor Vehicles banned its vehicles from state freeway operations. The ban, which the DMV says began on November 11, comes after the department determined that Waymo ’s freeway driving poses “an imminent hazard to public safety.”
In response, Waymo says it has stopped highway driving in all of its markets. The company will continue to test its vehicles on highways with safety operators behind the wheel.
The ban follows two recent concerning incidents, California DMV spokesperson Jonathan Groveman wrote in a statement. In one, three Waymos entered an active highway construction closure on Route 101 on the San Francisco Peninsula. The other was captured in a viral video showing a Waymo vehicle interfering with California Highway Patrol cars on a San Francisco highway as they tried to enforce a “traffic break” as workers cleared debris from a crash.
Groveman said the California ban will remain in place until Waymo has proved that it has “taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies” that led to the incidents. It’s unclear how long that process will take.
In a written statement to WIRED, Waymo spokesperson Dana Gallagher said the company is “working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.” Waymo vehicles will continue to operate on surface streets in the 15 metros where it offers taxi service, including portions of Los Angeles, San Diego, and the San Francisco Bay Area.
This is the second time Waymo has publicly restricted its freeway operations after beginning to transport passengers on them last year . In June, the company recalled its software after federal regulators found that its system failed to recognize highway construction zones. Regulators with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration cited several incidents in April and May in which Waymo cars drove past ramp closure signs and into active lane closures. The events did not lead to collisions or injuries.
The NHTSA did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Last week, the agency said it was examining whether another Waymo recall software fix had actually solved its robotaxis’ safety issues. This recall, which occurred last December, was tied to incidents in which Waymo cars repeatedly drove by stopped school buses with their lights on and/or stop arms extended .
Self-driving cars have struggled with construction zones for at least a decade . The zones can look and be arranged differently based on what sort of construction is being done and where. While humans can easily understand bollards, placards, and blinking arrows, the lack of hard-and-fast rules has proven difficult to reliably program into driving software. The issue is especially hazardous at freeway speeds, where workers exist alongside fast-moving car traffic.
Update, November 17 at 7pm: This story was updated to include more detail about Waymo’s plans to continue testing its vehicles on highways with drivers behind the wheel, per a statement from the company.

Şirkete göre her iki model de önceki sürümlere kıyasla daha az token kullanarak karmaşık görevleri tamamlayabiliyor.
GPT-6.2 Astra'nın özellikle sunum, elektronik tablo ve doküman hazırlama konusunda önemli iyileştirmeler sunduğu belirtiliyor. Model, verilen şablonları daha yakından takip edebiliyor ve hazırladığı içerikleri hukuk, finans, satış ve muhasebe gibi farklı alanların çalışma biçimlerine göre şekillendirebiliyor.OpenAI, modelin daha doğrudan metinler oluşturduğunu ve genel ifadeler ile gereksiz ayrıntıları azaltmayı hedeflediğini ifade ediyor.
Sunum hazırlama tarafında Astra, kendisine verilen mevcut bir dosyayı veya yalnızca bir ekran görüntüsünü referans alabiliyor. Model, düzen, renkler ve yazı boyutları gibi unsurları analiz ederek aynı tasarım dilini yeni slaytlara taşıyabiliyor.
GPT-6.2 Astra'nın kodlama yetenekleri de geliştirilmiş durumda. OpenAI'a göre model, m evcut kod tabanlarında karmaşık değişiklikler yapma ve bu değişiklikleri test etme konusunda önceki sürümlere kıyasla daha başarılı. Erken dönem kullanıcılarının daha temiz kod yapısı, daha odaklı testler ve daha az revizyon ihtiyacı ile karşılaştığı belirtiliyor.
Modelin geliştirme alanlarından biri de bilgisayar kullanımı ve 3D tasarım . OpenAI, Astra'nın CAD ve simülasyon araçlarında parçalar ve bağlantılar üzerinde daha hassas çalışabildiğini belirtiyor. Şirket ayrıca modelin mekanik sistemleri parça parça modelleyebildiğini ve tasarım değişikliklerinin sistem üzerindeki etkilerini incelemek için kullanılabileceğini ifade ediyor.
GPT-6.2 Sol ise OpenAI'ın günlük teknik ve teknik olmayan işler için önerdiği model olarak konumlanıyor. Model; çok adımlı ajan iş akışlarını gerçekleştirme, kod yazma ve doğal metin üretme gibi görevlerde kullanılabiliyor. OpenAI, şirket çalışanlarının da Sol'u günlük çalışmalarında sıklıkla tercih ettiğini belirtiyor. Sol'un dikkat çeken taraflarından biri Astra'ya kıyasla daha düşük maliyetle benzer kodlama performansına yaklaşabilmesi.
Gerçek kod tabanlarında yapılan değişikliklerin kullanıma hazır olup olmadığını ölçen FrontierCode 2.0 testinde GPT-6.2 Sol, en yüksek akıl yürütme seviyesinde Astra'nın yaklaşık yarım puan gerisinde kalırken maliyetinin yaklaşık beşte biri seviyesinde gerçekleşti.
Yeni modellerle birlikte OpenAI, Ultrafast adını verdiği yüksek hızlı çalışma seçeneğinin erişimini de genişletiyor. Pro 500 aboneleri hem GPT-6.2 Astra hem de GPT-6.2 Sol'u Ultrafast ile kullanabilirken, Pro 200 aboneleri ilk kez GPT-6.2 Sol ile bu seçeneğe erişebiliyor. OpenAI'a göre Ultrafast, standart çalışma hızına kıyasla token üretimini 4,5 kata kadar hızlandırabiliyor ancak kullanıcının kullanım kotasını daha hızlı tüketiyor.
GPT-6.2 Astra ve Sol'un şu aşamada normal ChatGPT sohbetlerindeki model seçicisine eklenmediğini belirtelim. Modellerin dağıtımı ChatGPT Work ve Codex üzerinden gerçekleştiriliyor ve erişim kullanıcının abonelik planına, çalışma alanı izinlerine ve dağıtım sürecine bağlı olarak değişebiliyor.
Geliştiriciler GPT-6.2 Astra ve GPT-6.2 Sol'a OpenAI API üzerinden de erişebiliyor. GPT-6.2 Astra'nın standart API fiyatı, GPT-6 Astra'ya kıyasla yüzde 20 düşürüldü . Modelin 1 milyon token başına girdi fiyatı 8 dolar , önbelleğe alınmış girdi fiyatı 0,40 dolar , çıktı fiyatı ise 40 dolar olarak belirlendi. GPT-6.2 Sol ise GPT-6.1 Sol ile aynı fiyatlandırmayı koruyor. Modelde 1 milyon token için girdi fiyatı 2 dolar, önbelleğe alınmış girdi 0,10 dolar , çıktı ise 10 dolar olarak açıklandı.
OpenAI ayrıca her iki modelin siber güvenlik yeteneklerinde de önemli ilerlemeler kaydettiğini belirtiyor. Modeller, güvenlik açıklarını tespit etme ve güvenli kod yazma konusunda daha gelişmiş yetenekler sunuyor. Ayrıca tespit edilen güvenlik açıklarının giderilmesine yönelik çözümler üretebiliyor. OpenAI, bu yeteneklerin kötüye kullanılmasını önlemek amacıyla yüksek riskli siber güvenlik taleplerine yönelik daha sıkı güvenlik önlemleri uyguluyor.

The Maytag Man is one of the most enduring characters in American advertising, lonely because no one needs his help repairing a Maytag appliance. The Maytag brand, too, has endured—dating back to the days when Frederick Maytag’s washers used wooden tubs and cranks. Maytag was the first company to put an agitator at the bottom of a washing machine, a design still in use today. It was also the first to stack a washer and dryer and one of the earliest adopters of smart appliances . But mostly, the brand has eschewed novelty and staked its claim on durability and reliability for its heavy-duty dishwashers, washers, dryers, refrigerators, and ovens. This is true even as Maytag came under the ownership of former competitor Whirlpool.
Maytag remains one of the few appliance companies to offer 10-year limited warranties on essential parts . Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for stronger global cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade, as he opened the APEC summit in Shenzhen ahead of an expected meeting with US President Donald Trump. Trade tensions and new US chip export restrictions are set to feature prominently.
Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for greater international cooperation on AI and free trade, as pressure grows on world powers to do more to address the risks of the groundbreaking technology.
Xi made the remarks as he formally opened an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, where he is expected to meet US President Donald Trump on Thursday.
"We should actively build partnerships for scientific and technological innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence and promote a green and low-carbon transition," the Chinese leader said.
"By continuously transforming our innovation strengths into growth momentum, we can provide a robust impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and foster shared prosperity across the region."
Read more China to host first-ever trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin next week
Xi also called for the elimination of trade and investment barriers, saying that it was crucial to "promote inclusive and balanced development".
He said China sought to "provide a more stable, predictable and beneficial environment for global enterprises" and would continue to expand access in its manufacturing and services sectors.
"Starting by lowering tariffs , expanding access and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform," Xi said.
Trade tensions have been looming over the leaders of the world's two largest economies as the summit has approached.
Trump has upended the global trade order by imposing wide-ranging tariffs on many countries, which China has met head-on with counter-levies and threats to withhold crucial exports.
Read more Xi, Trump and Putin to discuss 'world peace' at Shenzhen summit, China says
On the sidelines of last year's APEC summit in South Korea , Trump and Xi reached a tenuous truce in their trade war, but it will expire in January.
The United States this week announced tougher restrictions on the export to China of advanced semiconductors used to train and run AI models, controls it says are needed for national security.
The new US rules crack down on chip smuggling, but also the large grey market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres in third countries full of chips designed by the Californian giant Nvidia.
Nvidia on Wednesday reported blockbuster earnings but the results were overshadowed by a widening scandal sparked by former CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman suspected by US officials of spying for China.
